usage.zh: 这是一个动词短语，'carry out' 表示执行、实施，后接名词 'repairs'。常用于正式或半正式语境，描述机构或人员正在进行的工作。注意 'carry out' 是及物动词短语，需要宾语。
usage.en: This is a verb phrase; 'carry out' means to perform or execute, followed by the noun 'repairs'. It is common in formal or semi-formal contexts to describe work being done by an organization or person. Note that 'carry out' is transitive and requires an object.

example.zh: 市政会本周正在对桥梁进行维修。
example.en: The council is carrying out repairs on the bridge this week.

meaning.en: not knowing about or not realizing something

usage.zh: 'unaware of' 后接名词或名词短语，表示对某事不知情。常用于正式或书面语。注意不要与 'unaware that' 混淆，后者接从句。
usage.en: 'Unaware of' is followed by a noun or noun phrase, meaning not knowing about something. It is common in formal or written English. Do not confuse it with 'unaware that', which is followed by a clause.

example.zh: 许多居民不知道新的停车规定。
example.en: Many residents were unaware of the new parking regulations.

meaning.en: on the condition that; if

usage.zh: 'provided that' 用于引导条件状语从句，表示只有在某种条件下某事才会发生。比 'if' 更正式，常用于书面语。注意从句中的时态通常用一般现在时表示将来。
usage.en: 'Provided that' introduces a conditional clause, meaning something will happen only under a certain condition. It is more formal than 'if' and common in written English. Note that the clause often uses the present simple for future meaning.

collocations: provided that the weather is good
provided that all conditions are met

example.zh: 如果我们获得足够的资金，我们就会继续举办这个活动。
example.en: We will go ahead with the event provided that we receive enough funding.

meaning.en: done after something else, often to check or add information

usage.zh: 'follow-up' 作形容词时，修饰名词，表示后续的、跟进的。常用于商务或正式沟通中，如 'follow-up email'、'follow-up meeting'。注意连字符的使用。
usage.en: As an adjective, 'follow-up' modifies a noun to indicate something done after an initial action, often to check or add information. It is common in business or formal communication, e.g., 'follow-up email', 'follow-up meeting'. Note the hyphen.

example.zh: 我发了一条后续消息来确认细节。
example.en: I sent a follow-up message to confirm the details.

meaning.en: official permission or agreement

usage.zh: 'approval' 是不可数名词，表示正式的批准或同意。常用于 'wait for approval'、'seek approval' 等短语中。注意与 'agreement' 的区别，'approval' 更强调官方或权威的认可。
usage.en: 'Approval' is an uncountable noun meaning official permission or agreement. It is often used in phrases like 'wait for approval' or 'seek approval'. Note the difference from 'agreement': 'approval' implies a more official or authoritative endorsement.

example.zh: 没有经理的批准，我们不能继续。
example.en: We cannot proceed without the manager's approval.

meaning.en: to deal with or take responsibility for something

usage.zh: 'handle' 是及物动词，表示处理或负责某事。在商务或正式语境中常用，如 'handle a task'、'handle a situation'。注意不要与 'deal with' 混淆，'handle' 更强调主动承担责任。
usage.en: 'Handle' is a transitive verb meaning to deal with or take responsibility for something. It is common in business or formal contexts, e.g., 'handle a task', 'handle a situation'. Do not confuse it with 'deal with'; 'handle' emphasizes taking active responsibility.

example.zh: 她将负责会议的所有安排。
example.en: She will handle all the arrangements for the conference.

prompt.zh: 在这一虚构情境中，你想邀请朋友 Jamie 初夏来镇上住两天。你有空房间可供住宿，并希望一起去本地博物馆与河畔公园。写信给 Jamie：①发出邀请并解释为何期待见面；②介绍住宿与可考虑的活动；③询问合适日期以及朋友想做什么。尚未订日期或门票，不编造价格、地址或确定营业时间。使用亲切的非正式语气，不少于 150 词，以 Dear Jamie, 开头。

title.zh: 非正式信：邀请朋友来访
title.en: Informal Letter: Inviting a Friend to Visit

segments.low: Dear Jamie, I hope you are well.
segments.high: Dear Jamie, I hope you're doing well.

note.zh: 将“I hope you are well”改为更口语化的“I hope you're doing well”，使用缩略形式和进行时，语气更亲切自然。
note.en: Changes 'I hope you are well' to the more conversational 'I hope you're doing well', using a contraction and progressive form for a friendlier tone.

expressionEdits.before: I hope you are well
expressionEdits.after: I hope you're doing well

explanation.zh: 缩略形式和进行时使问候更随意自然，适合朋友间的信件。
explanation.en: The contraction and progressive form make the greeting more casual and natural for a friend.

translationZh.low: 亲爱的杰米，希望你一切都好。
translationZh.high: 亲爱的杰米，希望你一切都好。

segments.low: I want to invite you to come to my town for two days in early summer.
segments.high: I'd love for you to visit my town for a couple of days in early summer.

note.zh: 用“I'd love for you to”替代“I want to invite you to”，表达更热情；用“a couple of days”替代“two days”，更口语化。
note.en: Replaces 'I want to invite you to' with 'I'd love for you to' for a warmer tone, and 'two days' with 'a couple of days' for a more conversational feel.

expressionEdits.before: I want to invite you to come to my town for two days
expressionEdits.after: I'd love for you to visit my town for a couple of days

explanation.zh: “I'd love for you to”比“I want to invite you to”更热情友好；“a couple of days”比“two days”更自然口语化。
explanation.en: 'I'd love for you to' is warmer and friendlier than 'I want to invite you to'; 'a couple of days' is more natural and conversational than 'two days'.

translationZh.low: 我想邀请你初夏来我的小镇住两天。
translationZh.high: 我很想让你初夏来我的小镇玩几天。

segments.low: It would be so nice to see you and spend time together.
segments.high: It would be wonderful to catch up and enjoy some time together.

note.zh: 用“wonderful”替代“so nice”，用“catch up”替代“spend time together”，表达更生动，体现对相聚的期待。
note.en: Replaces 'so nice' with 'wonderful' and 'spend time together' with 'catch up' to sound more vivid and show anticipation.

translationZh.low: 见到你并一起度过时光会很好。
translationZh.high: 能叙叙旧并一起享受时光会很棒。

segments.low: I really enjoy your company and I miss our talks. I think we can have a fun and relaxing time here.
segments.high: I always enjoy your company and miss our conversations, so I'm sure we'd have a fun and relaxing visit.

note.zh: 将两个短句合并为一句，用“so”连接因果关系，使逻辑更连贯；用“I'm sure”替代“I think”，语气更肯定。
note.en: Combines two short sentences into one using 'so' to show cause and effect, improving cohesion; replaces 'I think' with 'I'm sure' for more certainty.

translationZh.low: 我真的很喜欢你的陪伴，我想念我们的交谈。我觉得我们在这里可以度过有趣而轻松的时光。
translationZh.high: 我一直很喜欢你的陪伴，想念我们的交谈，所以我确信我们会度过有趣而轻松的访问。

segments.low: You can stay in my spare room. It is comfortable and has a bed and a small desk. You will have your own space.
segments.high: You're welcome to stay in my spare room, which is comfortable and has a bed and a small desk, so you'd have your own space.

note.zh: 将三个短句合并为一个复合句，使用定语从句和结果状语从句，使信息更紧凑，逻辑更清晰。
note.en: Combines three short sentences into one complex sentence using a relative clause and a result clause, making the information more compact and logical.

translationZh.low: 你可以住我的空房间。它很舒适，有一张床和一张小书桌。你会有自己的空间。
translationZh.high: 欢迎你住我的空房间，它很舒适，有一张床和一张小书桌，所以你会有自己的空间。

segments.low: We could visit the local museum. It has many interesting things about our town history. Also we can go to the riverside park.
segments.high: We could visit the local museum, which has some interesting exhibits about the town's history, and then take a walk in the riverside park.

note.zh: 用定语从句合并前两句，并用“and then”连接活动，使行程描述更连贯；“exhibits”比“things”更准确。
note.en: Uses a relative clause to combine the first two sentences and 'and then' to link activities, making the description more cohesive; 'exhibits' is more precise than 'things'.

translationZh.low: 我们可以参观当地博物馆。它有很多关于我们小镇历史的有趣东西。我们也可以去河畔公园。
translationZh.high: 我们可以参观当地博物馆，那里有一些关于小镇历史的有趣展品，然后去河畔公园散步。

segments.low: We can walk by the river and maybe have a picnic if the weather is nice.
segments.high: We might stroll along the river and perhaps have a picnic if the weather is pleasant.

note.zh: 用“might stroll”替代“can walk”，用“pleasant”替代“nice”，词汇更丰富，语气更委婉。
note.en: Replaces 'can walk' with 'might stroll' and 'nice' with 'pleasant', using richer vocabulary and a more tentative tone.

expressionEdits.before: We can walk by the river
expressionEdits.after: We might stroll along the river

explanation.zh: “stroll”比“walk”更悠闲；“might”比“can”更委婉，符合建议语气。
explanation.en: 'Stroll' is more leisurely than 'walk'; 'might' is more tentative than 'can', suiting a suggestion.

translationZh.low: 如果天气好，我们可以沿河散步，也许野餐。
translationZh.high: 如果天气宜人，我们可能沿河漫步，也许野餐。

segments.low: Do you have any dates in early summer that work for you?
segments.high: Are there any dates in early summer that would suit you?

note.zh: 用“Are there any dates... that would suit you?”替代“Do you have any dates... that work for you?”，表达更正式礼貌，适合询问。
note.en: Replaces 'Do you have any dates... that work for you?' with 'Are there any dates... that would suit you?', which is more formal and polite for asking.

translationZh.low: 初夏你有合适的日期吗？
translationZh.high: 初夏有没有适合你的日期？

segments.low: I can take time off work to show you around.
segments.high: I can arrange time off work to show you around.

note.zh: 用“arrange time off”替代“take time off”，强调主动安排，表达更周到。
note.en: Replaces 'take time off' with 'arrange time off', emphasizing proactive planning and sounding more considerate.

expressionEdits.before: I can take time off work
expressionEdits.after: I can arrange time off work

explanation.zh: “arrange”暗示会提前计划，比“take”更显主动和体贴。
explanation.en: 'Arrange' implies planning ahead, which is more proactive and considerate than 'take'.

translationZh.low: 我可以请假带你四处看看。
translationZh.high: 我可以安排请假带你四处看看。

segments.low: Tell me if there is anything special you want to do. We can plan together.
segments.high: Let me know if there's anything in particular you'd like to do, and we can plan the days together.

note.zh: 将两个句子合并为一句，用“and”连接；用“in particular”替代“special”，表达更自然；补充“the days”使指代更明确。
note.en: Combines two sentences into one using 'and'; replaces 'special' with 'in particular' for a more natural phrase; adds 'the days' for clarity.

translationZh.low: 告诉我你有没有什么特别想做的。我们可以一起计划。
translationZh.high: 告诉我你有没有特别想做的事，我们可以一起计划这几天。

segments.low: I am really looking forward to your reply. I hope you can come. Best wishes, Alex
segments.high: I'm really looking forward to hearing from you and hope you can make it. Best wishes, Alex

note.zh: 用“hearing from you”替代“your reply”，用“make it”替代“come”，表达更口语化、亲切。
note.en: Replaces 'your reply' with 'hearing from you' and 'come' with 'make it', making the closing more conversational and warm.

expressionEdits.before: I am really looking forward to your reply. I hope you can come
expressionEdits.after: I'm really looking forward to hearing from you and hope you can make it

explanation.zh: “hearing from you”比“your reply”更亲切；“make it”是口语中表示“能来”的常用表达。
explanation.en: 'Hearing from you' is warmer than 'your reply'; 'make it' is a common colloquial way to say 'come'.

translationZh.low: 我真的很期待你的回复。希望你能来。祝好，亚历克斯
translationZh.high: 我真的很期待收到你的来信，希望你能来。祝好，亚历克斯

note.zh: 高分版本更清晰地覆盖了三个要点：邀请并说明原因、描述住宿和活动、询问日期和偏好。语气热情友好，细节具体（如博物馆展品、河边散步、野餐）。低分版本也覆盖要点但表达较平淡，缺少对活动的具体描述。高分版本未编造价格或时间，符合要求。
note.en: The high version more clearly covers all three bullet points: inviting with reasons, describing accommodation and activities, and asking about dates and preferences. The tone is warm and friendly with specific details (museum exhibits, riverside walk, picnic). The low version covers the points but is plainer with less specific activity description. The high version does not invent prices or times, meeting the requirements.

note.zh: 高分版本通过使用连接词（so, and then）和合并短句，使段落内部和段落之间的逻辑更连贯。例如，将住宿描述合并为一个复合句，将活动描述用“and then”连接。低分版本句子较短，连接较少，但整体结构仍清晰。高分版本在连贯性上更胜一筹。
note.en: The high version improves cohesion by using connectors (so, and then) and combining short sentences, making the logic within and between paragraphs clearer. For example, the accommodation description is combined into one complex sentence, and activities are linked with 'and then'. The low version has shorter sentences and fewer connections, but the overall structure is still clear. The high version is superior in coherence.

note.zh: 高分版本使用了更丰富的词汇和表达，如“catch up”、“stroll”、“exhibits”、“in particular”、“make it”等，比低分版本的“spend time together”、“walk”、“things”、“special”、“come”更生动具体。同时，高分版本避免了重复，用词更精准。低分版本词汇较基础，但能满足任务要求。
note.en: The high version uses a wider range of vocabulary and expressions, such as 'catch up', 'stroll', 'exhibits', 'in particular', 'make it', which are more vivid and specific than the low version's 'spend time together', 'walk', 'things', 'special', 'come'. The high version also avoids repetition and uses more precise wording. The low version uses basic vocabulary but meets the task requirements.

note.zh: 高分版本展示了更复杂的语法结构，如定语从句（“which is comfortable...”）、结果状语从句（“so you'd have your own space”）和条件句（“if the weather is pleasant”）。低分版本主要使用简单句和并列句，语法正确但缺乏变化。高分版本在语法多样性和准确性上表现更好。
note.en: The high version demonstrates more complex grammatical structures, such as relative clauses ('which is comfortable...'), result clauses ('so you'd have your own space'), and conditional sentences ('if the weather is pleasant'). The low version mainly uses simple and compound sentences, which are grammatically correct but lack variety. The high version performs better in grammatical range and accuracy.

zh: 使用更具体的词汇（如 exhibits, stroll）替代泛泛之词，提升表达生动性。
通过合并短句和使用连接词（so, and then）增强段落连贯性。
在非正式信件中运用缩略形式和口语表达（I'd love, make it）使语气更亲切。
en: Use more specific vocabulary (e.g., exhibits, stroll) instead of general words to make writing more vivid.
Combine short sentences and use connectors (so, and then) to improve paragraph coherence.
Use contractions and colloquial expressions (I'd love, make it) in informal letters to sound friendlier.

taskAnalysis.zh: 本题要求写一封非正式邀请信，邀请朋友初夏来访两天。需包含三点：邀请并解释期待原因；描述住宿和活动；询问日期与朋友偏好。语气应亲切自然，不少于150词，不编造具体信息。
taskAnalysis.en: This task requires an informal invitation letter to a friend for a two-day visit in early summer. It must cover three points: inviting and explaining why you look forward to the visit; describing accommodation and activities; asking about dates and preferences. The tone should be friendly and natural, at least 150 words, with no invented specifics.

role.zh: 开头问候并发出邀请，表达期待见面的心情。
role.en: Opening greeting and invitation, expressing eagerness to meet.

analysis.zh: 低分版本以标准问候开头，用'I want to invite you'直接邀请，随后说明喜欢陪伴和想念交谈，但句子略显生硬。高分版本用'I'd love for you to visit'更自然亲切，'wonderful to catch up'和'always enjoy your company'更流畅地传达情感，整体语气更温暖友好。
analysis.en: The low version opens with a standard greeting and uses 'I want to invite you' directly, then mentions enjoying company and missing talks, but the sentences feel slightly stiff. The high version uses 'I'd love for you to visit' which is more natural and warm, and 'wonderful to catch up' and 'always enjoy your company' convey the sentiment more smoothly, making the tone friendlier.

role.zh: 介绍住宿安排和计划的活动。
role.en: Describing accommodation and planned activities.

analysis.zh: 低分版本用简单句逐一说明空余房间和博物馆、公园，信息完整但缺乏连贯性。高分版本用定语从句和连接词将信息整合，如'which is comfortable...'和'which has some interesting exhibits...'，使句子更流畅，同时用'stroll'和'pleasant'提升词汇丰富度。
analysis.en: The low version lists the spare room, museum, and park in simple sentences, which is clear but lacks flow. The high version integrates information using relative clauses and connectors like 'which is comfortable...' and 'which has some interesting exhibits...', making sentences smoother, while using 'stroll' and 'pleasant' for better vocabulary.

role.zh: 询问合适日期和朋友想做的活动。
role.en: Asking about suitable dates and activities the friend would like to do.

analysis.zh: 低分版本用'Do you have any dates...'和'Tell me if...'直接提问，虽清晰但略显生硬。高分版本用'Are there any dates...'和'Let me know if...'更礼貌自然，'that would suit you'比'that work for you'更正式友好，'arrange time off work'比'take time off work'稍显主动。
analysis.en: The low version uses 'Do you have any dates...' and 'Tell me if...' which are direct and clear but a bit abrupt. The high version uses 'Are there any dates...' and 'Let me know if...' which are more polite and natural, 'that would suit you' is friendlier than 'that work for you', and 'arrange time off work' sounds more proactive than 'take time off work'.

role.zh: 结尾表达期待回复和见面。
role.en: Closing with anticipation of a reply and meeting.

analysis.zh: 低分版本以'I am really looking forward to your reply. I hope you can come.'结束，虽然正确但略显重复。高分版本用'I'm really looking forward to hearing from you and hope you can make it.'更简洁流畅，'make it'是口语化表达，更符合非正式信件语气。
analysis.en: The low version ends with 'I am really looking forward to your reply. I hope you can come.' which is correct but slightly repetitive. The high version uses 'I'm really looking forward to hearing from you and hope you can make it.' which is more concise and fluid, with 'make it' being a colloquial expression that suits the informal tone.

title.zh: 使用更自然的邀请表达
title.en: Using more natural invitation expressions

explanation.zh: 高分版本用'I'd love for you to visit'代替低分版本的'I want to invite you'。'I'd love for you to...'是更亲切、更地道的邀请方式，表达强烈愿望而非单纯意图，使语气更温暖友好。
explanation.en: The high version uses 'I'd love for you to visit' instead of the low version's 'I want to invite you'. 'I'd love for you to...' is a warmer and more idiomatic way to invite, expressing strong desire rather than mere intention, making the tone friendlier.

title.zh: 用定语从句整合信息
title.en: Integrating information with relative clauses

explanation.zh: 高分版本在描述房间和博物馆时使用定语从句，如'which is comfortable and has a bed...'和'which has some interesting exhibits...'，将两个简单句合并为一个流畅的句子，提升连贯性和复杂度。
explanation.en: The high version uses relative clauses when describing the room and museum, such as 'which is comfortable and has a bed...' and 'which has some interesting exhibits...', merging two simple sentences into one smooth sentence, improving coherence and complexity.

title.zh: 选择更精确的动词
title.en: Choosing more precise verbs

explanation.zh: 高分版本用'stroll'代替'walk'，'stroll'表示悠闲地散步，更符合与朋友在河边放松的情境；用'arrange'代替'take'，'arrange time off work'暗示主动安排，比'take time off work'更显周到。
explanation.en: The high version uses 'stroll' instead of 'walk', as 'stroll' implies a leisurely walk, fitting the relaxed riverside context; and 'arrange' instead of 'take', as 'arrange time off work' suggests proactive planning, more considerate than 'take time off work'.

mistakes.zh: 低分版本中'It would be so nice to see you and spend time together.'虽然正确，但'It would be so nice'略显平淡，高分版本改为'It would be wonderful to catch up and enjoy some time together.'，'wonderful'和'catch up'更生动地表达期待。
mistakes.en: In the low version, 'It would be so nice to see you and spend time together.' is correct but 'It would be so nice' is a bit bland; the high version changes it to 'It would be wonderful to catch up and enjoy some time together.', where 'wonderful' and 'catch up' express anticipation more vividly.

mistakes.zh: 低分版本中'Tell me if there is anything special you want to do.'语气略显直接，高分版本改为'Let me know if there's anything in particular you'd like to do.'，'Let me know'和'in particular'更礼貌自然。
mistakes.en: In the low version, 'Tell me if there is anything special you want to do.' sounds a bit direct; the high version changes it to 'Let me know if there's anything in particular you'd like to do.', where 'Let me know' and 'in particular' are more polite and natural.

meaning.en: to talk to someone you have not seen for some time and find out about their life

usage.zh: 非正式用语，常用于朋友间。通常不带宾语或接'with someone'。注意不要与'catch up on'（补做某事）混淆。
usage.en: Informal, used among friends. Often used without an object or with 'with someone'. Do not confuse with 'catch up on' (to do something you have not done).

collocations: catch up with an old friend
have a lot to catch up on

example.zh: 和你喝咖啡叙旧真是太好了。
example.en: It was great to catch up with you over coffee.

meaning.en: the fact of being with someone else, especially in a way that provides friendship and enjoyment

usage.zh: 不可数名词，表示'陪伴'时常用'enjoy someone's company'。注意与'company'表示'公司'的意思区分。
usage.en: Uncountable noun; when meaning companionship, often used in 'enjoy someone's company'. Distinguish from 'company' meaning a business.

example.zh: 在这些活动中我总是很喜欢你的陪伴。
example.en: I always enjoy your company at these events.

meaning.en: objects or collections of objects put on show in a museum or gallery

usage.zh: 常用复数形式，指博物馆中的展品。单数'exhibit'也可指一件展品或展览。注意与'exhibition'（展览）区分。
usage.en: Often used in plural to refer to objects in a museum. Singular 'exhibit' can also be one object or a display. Distinguish from 'exhibition' (the event).

example.zh: 博物馆有一些关于当地历史的迷人展品。
example.en: The museum has some fascinating exhibits on local history.

meaning.en: to walk somewhere in a slow relaxed way

usage.zh: 不及物动词，常与'along'、'through'等介词连用。比'walk'更强调悠闲。名词形式为'stroll'，如'go for a stroll'。
usage.en: Intransitive verb, often used with prepositions like 'along' or 'through'. Emphasizes leisure more than 'walk'. Noun form is 'stroll', as in 'go for a stroll'.

example.zh: 我们漫步穿过公园，享受着阳光。
example.en: We strolled through the park, enjoying the sunshine.

meaning.en: enjoyable, attractive, friendly, or easy to like

usage.zh: 常用于描述天气、环境或经历。比'nice'稍正式，但仍在非正式场合使用。可修饰名词或作表语。
usage.en: Commonly used to describe weather, surroundings, or experiences. Slightly more formal than 'nice' but still used informally. Can modify a noun or be predicative.

example.zh: 我们在湖边度过了一个愉快的下午。
example.en: We had a pleasant afternoon by the lake.

meaning.en: to be able to be present at a particular event or place

usage.zh: 非正式用语，常用于表示能否参加活动。注意与'make it'表示'成功'的用法区分，此处特指'能来'。
usage.en: Informal, often used to indicate ability to attend an event. Distinguish from 'make it' meaning 'to succeed'; here it means 'to come'.

example.zh: 我很高兴你能来参加聚会。
example.en: I'm glad you could make it to the reunion.

prompt.zh: 在这一虚构情境中，朋友 Chris 同意借自行车给你购物。途中一个轮胎没气了，你立即停止骑行。写信给 Chris：①解释发生了什么；②道歉并说明补救打算；③询问维修和归还方案是否方便。你计划修好再还，但尚未预约，也未确认原因或费用。不要编造事故或其他损坏。使用体贴的非正式语气，不少于 150 词，以 Dear Chris, 开头。

title.zh: 非正式信：借来的自行车爆胎
title.en: Informal Letter: Apologising About a Borrowed Bicycle

segments.low: Dear Chris, I want to say sorry about your bicycle. When I was riding to the shops, the front tyre went flat all of a sudden.
segments.high: Dear Chris, I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but while I was cycling to the shops the front tyre suddenly went flat.

note.zh: 低分版开头直接道歉但略显生硬，高分版用更自然的道歉表达并增加过渡，使语气更流畅。
note.en: The low version opens with a direct apology but sounds abrupt; the high version uses a more natural apology and adds a transition for smoother tone.

expressionEdits.before: I want to say sorry about your bicycle.
expressionEdits.after: I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but

explanation.zh: 将生硬的道歉改为更地道的表达，并增加连接词使句子更连贯。
explanation.en: Replaces a stiff apology with a more idiomatic phrase and adds a connector for better flow.

translationZh.low: 亲爱的 Chris，我想为你的自行车道歉。当我去商店的路上，前胎突然没气了。
translationZh.high: 亲爱的 Chris，我真的很抱歉必须告诉你这件事，但在我骑车去商店的路上，前胎突然没气了。

segments.low: I stopped riding straight away and pushed it home, so I don't think any more damage happened.
segments.high: I got off immediately and walked it back, so I'm hoping that prevented any further damage.

note.zh: 低分版用词较简单，高分版使用更精确的动词和更谨慎的表达，避免绝对化。
note.en: The low version uses simpler words; the high version employs more precise verbs and a more cautious expression, avoiding absolutes.

expressionEdits.before: stopped riding straight away and pushed it home
expressionEdits.after: got off immediately and walked it back

explanation.zh: 用更具体的动作描述替换笼统表达，使画面更生动。
explanation.en: Replaces vague description with more specific actions for vividness.

expressionEdits.before: I don't think any more damage happened
expressionEdits.after: I'm hoping that prevented any further damage

explanation.zh: 将不确定的否定改为积极的希望表达，语气更委婉且避免绝对判断。
explanation.en: Changes a negative uncertain statement to a positive hopeful one, softening tone and avoiding absolute judgment.

translationZh.low: 我立即停止骑行并推着它回家，所以我认为没有发生更多损坏。
translationZh.high: 我立刻下车并把它推回去，所以我希望这防止了进一步的损坏。

segments.low: I feel bad because you lent it to me for the shopping trip and now I couldn't finish what I planned.
segments.high: I feel awful, especially since you were kind enough to lend it to me for the shopping trip, and I wasn't able to complete my errands.

note.zh: 低分版表达平淡，高分版通过强调对方的善意和增加连接词，使歉意更真诚。
note.en: The low version is flat; the high version emphasizes the other's kindness and adds connectors, making the apology more sincere.

expressionEdits.before: because you lent it to me
expressionEdits.after: especially since you were kind enough to lend it to me

explanation.zh: 增加强调成分，突出对方的善意，增强情感色彩。
explanation.en: Adds emphasis to highlight the other's kindness, enhancing emotional tone.

expressionEdits.before: couldn't finish what I planned
expressionEdits.after: wasn't able to complete my errands

explanation.zh: 用更准确的词汇描述未完成的事情，提升表达精确度。
explanation.en: Uses more precise vocabulary to describe unfinished tasks, improving accuracy.

translationZh.low: 我感觉很糟，因为你把它借给我用于购物行程，而现在我无法完成我计划的事。
translationZh.high: 我感觉很糟，尤其是你那么好心把它借给我用于购物行程，而我无法完成我的差事。

segments.low: I plan to take it to a repair shop and get the tyre fixed before I give it back to you.
segments.high: My plan is to take it to a repair shop and have the tyre properly fixed before returning the bike to you.

note.zh: 低分版句子结构简单，高分版使用名词短语开头并添加副词，使表达更正式和完整。
note.en: The low version has a simple sentence structure; the high version starts with a noun phrase and adds an adverb, making it more formal and complete.

expressionEdits.before: I plan to take it to a repair shop
expressionEdits.after: My plan is to take it to a repair shop

explanation.zh: 将动词短语改为名词短语作主语，使句子更正式。
explanation.en: Changes a verb phrase to a noun phrase as subject, making the sentence more formal.

translationZh.low: 我计划把它送到修理店，在还给你之前把轮胎修好。
translationZh.high: 我的计划是把它送到修理店，在归还自行车之前把轮胎彻底修好。

segments.low: I haven't made a booking yet, but I will do it as soon as I can.
segments.high: I haven't booked it in anywhere yet, but I'll sort that out as soon as possible.

note.zh: 低分版表达笼统，高分版使用更地道的动词短语并加强语气，使表达更自然。
note.en: The low version is vague; the high version uses a more idiomatic verb phrase and stronger tone for naturalness.

translationZh.low: 我还没有预约，但我会尽快去做。
translationZh.high: 我还没有在任何地方预约，但我会尽快安排。

segments.low: I will pay for the repair myself, of course.
segments.high: Naturally, I'll cover the cost of the repair myself.

note.zh: 低分版用词平淡，高分版将副词前置并更换动词，使语气更坚定且句子更流畅。
note.en: The low version is plain; the high version front-loads the adverb and changes the verb, making tone firmer and sentence smoother.

translationZh.low: 我当然会自己支付修理费用。
translationZh.high: 当然，我会自己承担修理费用。

segments.low: Could you let me know if this plan is convenient for you?
segments.high: Would it be convenient for you if I get it repaired and then bring it back?

note.zh: 低分版直接询问计划，高分版使用条件句具体说明方案，使请求更清晰。
note.en: The low version asks directly about the plan; the high version uses a conditional sentence to specify the arrangement, making the request clearer.

translationZh.low: 你能告诉我这个计划对你是否方便吗？
translationZh.high: 如果我把它修好然后带回来，对你来说方便吗？

segments.low: If you need the bicycle back quickly, please tell me and I will try to do the repair faster.
segments.high: If you need the bike back urgently, just let me know and I'll try to speed up the repair.

note.zh: 低分版用词冗余，高分版使用更简洁地道的表达，使语气更直接。
note.en: The low version is wordy; the high version uses more concise and idiomatic expressions, making tone more direct.

expressionEdits.before: If you need the bicycle back quickly, please tell me
expressionEdits.after: If you need the bike back urgently, just let me know

explanation.zh: 替换词汇并简化结构，使表达更自然流畅。
explanation.en: Replaces vocabulary and simplifies structure for more natural flow.

expressionEdits.before: I will try to do the repair faster
expressionEdits.after: I'll try to speed up the repair

explanation.zh: 使用动词短语使表达更简洁有力。
explanation.en: Uses a phrasal verb for conciseness and impact.

translationZh.low: 如果你需要尽快拿回自行车，请告诉我，我会尝试更快地修理。
translationZh.high: 如果你急需自行车，就告诉我，我会尽量加快修理。

segments.low: Maybe we can arrange a time for me to return it after it is fixed.
segments.high: Perhaps we can agree on a time for me to drop it off once it's been fixed.

note.zh: 低分版表达较啰嗦，高分版使用更简洁的动词和短语，使句子更紧凑。
note.en: The low version is wordy; the high version uses more concise verbs and phrases, making the sentence tighter.

expressionEdits.before: arrange a time for me to return it
expressionEdits.after: agree on a time for me to drop it off

explanation.zh: 用更具体的动词短语替换笼统表达，提升准确性。
explanation.en: Replaces vague expression with a more specific phrasal verb, improving accuracy.

translationZh.low: 也许我们可以在它修好后安排一个时间让我归还。
translationZh.high: 也许我们可以商定一个时间，在它修好后我把它送回去。

segments.low: I am sorry again for the trouble.
segments.high: Once again, I'm really sorry for the hassle.

note.zh: 低分版道歉简短，高分版使用更完整的句子和强调副词，使歉意更恳切。
note.en: The low version has a brief apology; the high version uses a fuller sentence and an intensifier, making the apology more earnest.

translationZh.low: 再次为麻烦道歉。
translationZh.high: 再次，我真的很抱歉给你带来麻烦。

segments.low: I hope it didn't cause you any problem.
segments.high: I hope this hasn't inconvenienced you too much.

note.zh: 低分版用词笼统，高分版使用更精确的名词并调整程度，使表达更得体。
note.en: The low version uses a vague word; the high version uses a more precise noun and adjusts degree, making expression more appropriate.

translationZh.low: 我希望它没有给你带来任何问题。
translationZh.high: 我希望这没有给你带来太多不便。

segments.low: Best wishes, Alex
segments.high: All the best, Alex

note.zh: 低分版结尾较正式，高分版使用更非正式且友好的结束语，符合信件语气。
note.en: The low version has a more formal closing; the high version uses a more informal and friendly sign-off, matching the letter's tone.

expressionEdits.before: Best wishes
expressionEdits.after: All the best

explanation.zh: 更换为更常见的非正式结束语，使语气更亲切。
explanation.en: Replaces with a more common informal closing, making tone friendlier.

translationZh.low: 最好的祝愿，Alex
translationZh.high: 一切顺利，Alex

note.zh: 两版都涵盖了三个要点：解释经过、道歉并说明补救、询问是否方便。高分版在解释中更具体地描述了立即下车和推车，增强了任务完成度；低分版信息完整但表达较笼统。两版均未编造事故，符合要求。
note.en: Both versions cover the three bullet points: explaining what happened, apologizing and outlining remedy, and asking about convenience. The high version provides more specific details in the explanation, such as getting off immediately and walking the bike, enhancing task achievement; the low version is complete but more general. Neither invents an accident, meeting requirements.

note.zh: 两版都使用了基本的连接词和段落划分，逻辑清晰。高分版在句间使用更多过渡表达（如 'especially since', 'Naturally'），使衔接更流畅；低分版连接较简单，但整体连贯。结尾部分高分版更自然地收束。
note.en: Both versions use basic linking words and paragraphing with clear logic. The high version employs more transitional expressions between sentences (e.g., 'especially since', 'Naturally'), making cohesion smoother; the low version has simpler connections but remains coherent. The high version concludes more naturally.

note.zh: 高分版词汇更丰富且地道，如 'got off immediately', 'sort that out', 'cover the cost', 'speed up', 'drop it off', 'hassle' 等；低分版词汇较基础，如 'stopped riding', 'do it', 'pay for', 'do the repair faster', 'return it', 'trouble'。高分版避免了重复，提升了表达精确度。
note.en: The high version uses richer and more idiomatic vocabulary, such as 'got off immediately', 'sort that out', 'cover the cost', 'speed up', 'drop it off', 'hassle'; the low version uses more basic words like 'stopped riding', 'do it', 'pay for', 'do the repair faster', 'return it', 'trouble'. The high version avoids repetition and improves precision.

note.zh: 两版语法基本准确，但高分版句式更多样，如使用名词短语开头（'My plan is...'）、条件句（'Would it be convenient...'）和更复杂的结构；低分版以简单句为主，变化较少。高分版在时态和语态上更自然。
note.en: Both versions are grammatically accurate, but the high version has more varied sentence structures, such as noun phrase openings ('My plan is...'), conditionals ('Would it be convenient...'), and more complex constructions; the low version relies on simple sentences with less variety. The high version is more natural in tense and voice.

zh: 使用更地道的短语和动词（如 sort out, cover the cost）替代基础表达，提升词汇得分。
通过增加过渡词和变换句式（如条件句、名词短语开头）增强连贯性和语法多样性。
在道歉信中具体描述行动并保持委婉语气，同时确保覆盖所有任务要点。
en: Replace basic expressions with more idiomatic phrases and verbs (e.g., sort out, cover the cost) to boost lexical score.
Enhance cohesion and grammatical range by adding transitions and varying sentence structures (e.g., conditionals, noun phrase openings).
In apology letters, describe actions specifically and maintain a polite tone while covering all task points.

taskAnalysis.zh: 这是一道非正式书信题：向朋友解释所借自行车途中爆胎、立即停骑并推回；道歉并说明会自费送修且尽快办理；询问修好后再归还的方案是否方便，并回应对方可能的紧急需求。语气需体贴、自然，不编造事故或额外损坏。
taskAnalysis.en: This informal letter requires explaining to a friend that a borrowed bicycle got a flat tyre mid-trip, that you stopped immediately and walked it back; apologising and stating you will pay for and arrange a repair promptly; and asking whether the repair-then-return plan suits them, while acknowledging any urgency. Tone should be considerate and natural, without inventing accidents or extra damage.

role.zh: 开头解释事件：爆胎经过及你的立即处理。
role.en: Opening that explains the incident: how the tyre went flat and your immediate response.

analysis.zh: 低分版本开门见山道歉，但“I want to say sorry”略显生硬，且“all of a sudden”不如 suddenly 简洁。高分版本用“I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but...”引出坏消息，更自然委婉；第二句用“got off immediately and walked it back”比“stopped riding straight away and pushed it home”更贴切口语，且“I'm hoping that prevented any further damage”比“I don't think any more damage happened”语气更柔和、留有余地。
analysis.en: The low version opens directly but 'I want to say sorry' is slightly stiff, and 'all of a sudden' is less concise than 'suddenly'. The high version uses 'I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but...' to introduce bad news more naturally and politely; the second sentence uses 'got off immediately and walked it back' which is more idiomatic than 'stopped riding straight away and pushed it home', and 'I'm hoping that prevented any further damage' sounds more tentative and considerate than 'I don't think any more damage happened'.

role.zh: 表达歉意并说明补救计划：送修、自费、尽快安排。
role.en: Expressing regret and outlining the remedy plan: repair shop, paying yourself, arranging promptly.

analysis.zh: 低分版本表达了歉意，但“I feel bad”略显平淡，“I couldn't finish what I planned”不够具体。高分版本用“I feel awful”强化情感，“especially since you were kind enough to lend it to me”点明对方善意，更显体贴；“complete my errands”比“finish what I planned”更符合购物情境。补救计划中，低分版“get the tyre fixed”可用，但高分版“have the tyre properly fixed”强调“妥善修好”，更贴合题意；“booked it in anywhere”比“made a booking”更口语化；“I'll sort that out as soon as possible”比“I will do it as soon as I can”更自然；“Naturally, I'll cover the cost”比“I will pay for the repair myself, of course”更简洁有力。
analysis.en: The low version expresses regret but 'I feel bad' is somewhat flat and 'I couldn't finish what I planned' is vague. The high version uses 'I feel awful' for stronger emotion, and 'especially since you were kind enough to lend it to me' acknowledges the friend's kindness, showing more consideration; 'complete my errands' fits the shopping context better than 'finish what I planned'. In the remedy plan, 'get the tyre fixed' is acceptable, but 'have the tyre properly fixed' emphasises doing it thoroughly, aligning with the task; 'booked it in anywhere' is more colloquial than 'made a booking'; 'I'll sort that out as soon as possible' is more natural than 'I will do it as soon as I can'; 'Naturally, I'll cover the cost' is more concise and emphatic than 'I will pay for the repair myself, of course'.

role.zh: 询问方案是否方便，回应紧急需求，再次致歉并表达关心。
role.en: Asking if the plan is convenient, responding to urgency, apologising again and showing concern.

analysis.zh: 低分版本问题直接，但“Could you let me know if this plan is convenient for you?”略显正式，且“this plan”指代不够清晰。高分版本用“Would it be convenient for you if I get it repaired and then bring it back?”更具体、更口语化。紧急情况处理中，低分版“do the repair faster”可理解，但高分版“speed up the repair”更地道；“Perhaps we can agree on a time for me to drop it off once it's been fixed”比“Maybe we can arrange a time for me to return it after it is fixed”更自然，“drop it off”更符合归还自行车的情境。结尾低分版“I am sorry again for the trouble”和“I hope it didn't cause you any problem”略显重复且平淡，高分版“Once again, I'm really sorry for the hassle”和“I hope this hasn't inconvenienced you too much”用词更精准、语气更真诚。
analysis.en: The low version asks directly, but 'Could you let me know if this plan is convenient for you?' is slightly formal and 'this plan' is vague. The high version uses 'Would it be convenient for you if I get it repaired and then bring it back?' which is more specific and conversational. For urgency, 'do the repair faster' is understandable, but 'speed up the repair' is more idiomatic; 'Perhaps we can agree on a time for me to drop it off once it's been fixed' is more natural than 'Maybe we can arrange a time for me to return it after it is fixed', with 'drop it off' fitting the bike return context. At the end, the low version's 'I am sorry again for the trouble' and 'I hope it didn't cause you any problem' are repetitive and flat, while the high version's 'Once again, I'm really sorry for the hassle' and 'I hope this hasn't inconvenienced you too much' are more precise and sincere.

role.zh: 结束语。
role.en: Closing.

analysis.zh: 低分版本“Best wishes”虽可用，但高分版本“All the best”在朋友间更常见、更亲切，符合非正式语气。
analysis.en: The low version's 'Best wishes' is acceptable, but the high version's 'All the best' is more common and warmer between friends, fitting the informal tone.

title.zh: 用委婉句式引出坏消息
title.en: Using a softening phrase to introduce bad news

explanation.zh: 高分版本开头用“I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but...”先表达歉意再陈述事实，比低分版本直接说“I want to say sorry about your bicycle”更委婉、更符合向朋友报告不便之事的礼貌习惯。这种句式在非正式书信中能有效降低消息的冲击力，体现体贴。
explanation.en: The high version opens with 'I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but...' to express regret before stating the fact, which is more tactful and polite than the low version's direct 'I want to say sorry about your bicycle' when reporting an inconvenience to a friend. This structure softens the impact of bad news and shows consideration in informal letters.

title.zh: 使用口语化动词短语增强自然度
title.en: Using colloquial phrasal verbs for naturalness

explanation.zh: 高分版本多处使用口语化短语，如“walked it back”“sort that out”“drop it off”“speed up”，比低分版本的“pushed it home”“do it”“return it”“do the repair faster”更地道、更符合朋友间非正式交流。这些短语动词使语言更生动，避免生硬。
explanation.en: The high version uses several colloquial phrasal verbs such as 'walked it back', 'sort that out', 'drop it off', and 'speed up', which are more idiomatic and fitting for informal communication between friends than the low version's 'pushed it home', 'do it', 'return it', and 'do the repair faster'. These phrasal verbs make the language more vivid and less stiff.

title.zh: 用具体细节和情感词汇增强体贴度
title.en: Using specific details and emotional vocabulary to show consideration

explanation.zh: 高分版本通过“especially since you were kind enough to lend it to me”点明对方的善意，用“I feel awful”强化歉意，用“properly fixed”强调会妥善处理，比低分版本的“I feel bad”“get the tyre fixed”更具体、更显真诚。这种细节和情感词汇的运用使信件更温暖、更符合题目要求的体贴语气。
explanation.en: The high version highlights the friend's kindness with 'especially since you were kind enough to lend it to me', strengthens the apology with 'I feel awful', and emphasises thoroughness with 'properly fixed', which are more specific and sincere than the low version's 'I feel bad' and 'get the tyre fixed'. These details and emotional words make the letter warmer and more aligned with the task's requirement for a considerate tone.

mistakes.zh: 低分版本中“I want to say sorry about your bicycle”表达生硬，且“about your bicycle”指代不清，可能被理解为对自行车本身道歉而非对事件道歉。高分版本改为“I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but while I was cycling to the shops the front tyre suddenly went flat”，先道歉再说明事件，更自然、更清晰。
mistakes.en: In the low version, 'I want to say sorry about your bicycle' is stiff and 'about your bicycle' is ambiguous, possibly implying an apology for the bicycle itself rather than the incident. The high version changes it to 'I'm really sorry to have to tell you this, but while I was cycling to the shops the front tyre suddenly went flat', which apologises first and then explains the event, sounding more natural and clear.

mistakes.zh: 低分版本中“I couldn't finish what I planned”表达模糊，未具体说明未完成的是购物任务，且“what I planned”不够地道。高分版本改为“I wasn't able to complete my errands”，用“errands”一词准确指代购物等日常事务，更符合语境。
mistakes.en: In the low version, 'I couldn't finish what I planned' is vague, not specifying that the shopping errand was unfinished, and 'what I planned' is not very idiomatic. The high version changes it to 'I wasn't able to complete my errands', using 'errands' to precisely refer to shopping and similar daily tasks, fitting the context better.

meaning.en: to lose air pressure abruptly (of a tyre)

usage.zh: 用于描述轮胎在短时间内失去气压，通常与 tyre 连用。注意 went flat 是系表结构，flat 为形容词作表语；suddenly 修饰整个动作，表示突发性。
usage.en: Used to describe a tyre losing air pressure in a short time, typically with 'tyre'. Note that 'went flat' is a linking verb + adjective structure; 'suddenly' modifies the whole action to indicate abruptness.

collocations: suddenly went flat on the motorway

example.zh: 我上班迟到了，因为路上汽车轮胎突然没气了。
example.en: I was late for work because my car tyre suddenly went flat on the way.

meaning.zh: 把它（自行车）推着走回去
meaning.en: to push a bicycle while walking it back to a place

usage.zh: 表示推着自行车走回某处，比 pushed it home 更口语化。walk 在此为及物动词，it 指代自行车，back 表示返回方向。
usage.en: Means to push a bicycle while walking back to a place, more colloquial than 'pushed it home'. 'Walk' is transitive here, 'it' refers to the bike, and 'back' indicates the return direction.

collocations: walked it back to the shop

example.zh: 轮胎爆了之后，我把自行车推回了租赁点。
example.en: After the tyre burst, I walked the bike back to the rental station.

meaning.zh: 完成我的日常事务（如购物）
meaning.en: to finish one's routine tasks, such as shopping

usage.zh: errands 指外出办理的小事，如购物、取件等，常用复数。complete 比 finish 更正式，但在此搭配中自然。注意 errands 通常与 run、do、complete 等动词连用。
usage.en: 'Errands' refers to small tasks done outside, such as shopping or picking things up, usually plural. 'Complete' is slightly more formal than 'finish' but natural here. Note that 'errands' typically collocates with verbs like run, do, or complete.

example.zh: 我需要在商店关门前完成我的日常事务。
example.en: I need to complete my errands before the shops close.

meaning.en: repaired thoroughly or correctly

usage.zh: properly 强调修理的质量，表示不是临时凑合。fixed 是 fix 的过去分词，与 have something done 结构连用，表示让别人做某事。
usage.en: 'Properly' emphasises the quality of the repair, meaning not just a temporary fix. 'Fixed' is the past participle of 'fix', used with 'have something done' to indicate arranging for someone else to do it.

example.zh: 我会把笔记本电脑拿去给技术人员妥善修理。
example.en: I'll take the laptop to a technician to have it properly fixed.

meaning.en: to deal with or resolve a matter

usage.zh: 口语中常用，表示安排或解决问题。sort out 可分开使用，that 指代前文提到的预约维修。注意时态：I'll sort that out 表示将来打算。
usage.en: Common in spoken English, meaning to arrange or resolve something. 'Sort out' is separable, and 'that' refers to the previously mentioned booking. Note the tense: 'I'll sort that out' indicates a future intention.

example.zh: 别担心这一团乱，我会在客人到来前处理好的。
example.en: Don't worry about the mess; I'll sort that out before the guests arrive.

meaning.en: to make something happen faster

usage.zh: 表示加快进程，可及物或不及物。在此句中为及物，宾语是 the repair。比 do the repair faster 更简洁地道。
usage.en: Means to make something happen faster, can be transitive or intransitive. Here it is transitive with 'the repair' as object. More concise and idiomatic than 'do the repair faster'.

example.zh: 我们需要加快送货速度以赶上截止日期。
example.en: We need to speed up the delivery to meet the deadline.

prompt.zh: 在这一虚构情境中，你最近参加了社区中心的初学者烹饪小组，成员练习简单蔬菜菜肴并交流想法。朋友 Taylor 曾表示想学做饭。写信给 Taylor：①描述小组和活动；②说明为何喜欢这种学习方式；③邀请朋友试上一节，并询问有空的时间。下次时间、收费和剩余名额尚未核查，不要编造这些信息或健康效果。使用鼓励性的非正式语气，不少于 150 词，以 Dear Taylor, 开头。

title.zh: 非正式信：向朋友分享烹饪兴趣
title.en: Informal Letter: Sharing a New Cooking Hobby

segments.low: Dear Taylor, I join a cooking group at the community centre last month.
segments.high: Dear Taylor, I recently joined a beginner cooking group at the community centre.

note.zh: 低版本时态错误，且缺少“初学者”这一重要信息；高版本使用过去时并补充了小组性质。
note.en: The low version has a tense error and omits the key detail that the group is for beginners; the high version uses the past tense and adds this information.

expressionEdits.before: I join a cooking group at the community centre last month.
expressionEdits.after: I recently joined a beginner cooking group at the community centre.

explanation.zh: 将一般现在时改为过去时，并加入“最近”和“初学者”使信息更准确。
explanation.en: Changes the verb to past tense and adds 'recently' and 'beginner' for accuracy.

translationZh.low: 亲爱的泰勒，我上个月加入了一个烹饪小组在社区中心。
translationZh.high: 亲爱的泰勒，我最近加入了社区中心的一个初学者烹饪小组。

segments.low: We meet every week and practise simple vegetable dishes together.
segments.high: We meet weekly and practise simple vegetable dishes together.

note.zh: 高版本将“every week”简化为“weekly”，表达更简洁。
note.en: The high version replaces 'every week' with 'weekly' for conciseness.

expressionEdits.before: every week
expressionEdits.after: weekly

explanation.zh: 用副词“weekly”替代短语“every week”，更简洁自然。
explanation.en: Uses the adverb 'weekly' instead of the phrase 'every week' for a more concise and natural style.

translationZh.low: 我们每周见面，一起练习简单的蔬菜菜肴。
translationZh.high: 我们每周见面，一起练习简单的蔬菜菜肴。

segments.low: Everyone bring a recipe or idea, and we cook in small teams.
segments.high: Everyone brings a recipe or an idea, and we cook in small teams.

note.zh: 低版本主谓一致错误，且并列结构不平衡；高版本修正了动词形式并添加了冠词。
note.en: The low version has a subject-verb agreement error and an unbalanced parallel structure; the high version corrects the verb form and adds an article.

expressionEdits.before: Everyone bring a recipe or idea
expressionEdits.after: Everyone brings a recipe or an idea

explanation.zh: 修正主谓一致，并在“idea”前加冠词，使并列结构平行。
explanation.en: Corrects subject-verb agreement and adds an article before 'idea' to make the parallel structure balanced.

translationZh.low: 每个人带一个食谱或想法，我们分小组做饭。
translationZh.high: 每个人带一个食谱或一个想法，我们分小组做饭。

segments.low: Last time we make a tomato soup and roasted carrots.
segments.high: Last time we made tomato soup and roasted carrots.

note.zh: 低版本时态错误且冠词使用不当；高版本使用过去时并省略了不必要的冠词。
note.en: The low version has a tense error and incorrect article usage; the high version uses the past tense and omits the unnecessary article.

expressionEdits.before: we make a tomato soup
expressionEdits.after: we made tomato soup

explanation.zh: 将动词改为过去时，并去掉“tomato soup”前的不定冠词，因为汤通常不可数。
explanation.en: Changes the verb to past tense and removes the indefinite article before 'tomato soup', as soup is typically uncountable.

translationZh.low: 上次我们做了一个番茄汤和烤胡萝卜。
translationZh.high: 上次我们做了番茄汤和烤胡萝卜。

segments.low: After cooking, we taste the food and talk about what we can do better.
segments.high: After cooking, we taste the food and discuss what we could improve.

note.zh: 高版本用“discuss”和“improve”替代“talk about”和“do better”，表达更正式、准确。
note.en: The high version replaces 'talk about' and 'do better' with 'discuss' and 'improve', which are more formal and precise.

expressionEdits.before: talk about what we can do better
expressionEdits.after: discuss what we could improve

explanation.zh: 使用更正式的动词“discuss”和“improve”，并用“could”使语气更委婉。
explanation.en: Uses the more formal verbs 'discuss' and 'improve', and 'could' for a more tentative tone.

translationZh.low: 做饭后，我们品尝食物并谈论我们可以做得更好的地方。
translationZh.high: 做饭后，我们品尝食物并讨论我们可以改进的地方。

segments.low: I enjoy learning this way because it is not like reading a recipe alone.
segments.high: I enjoy learning this way because it is nothing like reading a recipe alone.

note.zh: 高版本用“nothing like”强化对比，使语气更生动。
note.en: The high version uses 'nothing like' to strengthen the contrast, making the tone more vivid.

expressionEdits.before: it is not like reading a recipe alone
expressionEdits.after: it is nothing like reading a recipe alone

explanation.zh: 用“nothing like”替代“not like”，强调差异程度。
explanation.en: Replaces 'not like' with 'nothing like' to emphasize the degree of difference.

translationZh.low: 我喜欢这样学习，因为这不像独自阅读食谱。
translationZh.high: 我喜欢这样学习，因为这完全不像独自阅读食谱。

segments.low: I can ask questions when I am not sure, and other people help me.
segments.high: I can ask questions whenever I am unsure, and others help me.

note.zh: 高版本用“whenever”和“unsure”替代“when”和“not sure”，更简洁且语法更正式。
note.en: The high version uses 'whenever' and 'unsure' instead of 'when' and 'not sure', which are more concise and grammatically formal.

translationZh.low: 当我不确定时，我可以问问题，其他人帮助我。
translationZh.high: 每当我不确定时，我可以问问题，其他人帮助我。

segments.low: Also, we share simple ideas, so I learn new ways to use vegetables.
segments.high: We also share simple ideas, so I pick up new ways to use vegetables.

note.zh: 高版本将“Also”移到句中，使衔接更流畅，并用“pick up”替代“learn”更口语化。
note.en: The high version moves 'also' into the sentence for smoother cohesion and uses 'pick up' instead of 'learn' for a more colloquial tone.

expressionEdits.before: Also, we share simple ideas, so I learn new ways
expressionEdits.after: We also share simple ideas, so I pick up new ways

explanation.zh: 调整“also”的位置使句子更自然，用短语动词“pick up”使表达更地道。
explanation.en: Adjusts the position of 'also' for a more natural sentence and uses the phrasal verb 'pick up' for a more idiomatic expression.

translationZh.low: 此外，我们分享简单的想法，所以我学会了使用蔬菜的新方法。
translationZh.high: 我们也分享简单的想法，所以我学会了使用蔬菜的新方法。

segments.low: I think you would like this group because you said you want to learn to cook. Would you like to try a session with me?
segments.high: I think you would enjoy this group because you mentioned wanting to learn to cook. Would you like to try a session with me?

note.zh: 高版本用“enjoy”替代“like”避免重复，用“mentioned”替代“said”更准确。
note.en: The high version replaces 'like' with 'enjoy' to avoid repetition and 'said' with 'mentioned' for greater accuracy.

expressionEdits.before: you would like this group because you said you want to learn to cook
expressionEdits.after: you would enjoy this group because you mentioned wanting to learn to cook

explanation.zh: 使用“enjoy”和“mentioned”使表达更精确，并将从句改为动名词结构。
explanation.en: Uses 'enjoy' and 'mentioned' for precision and changes the clause to a gerund structure.

translationZh.low: 我想你会喜欢这个小组，因为你说过你想学做饭。你想和我一起试一节课吗？
translationZh.high: 我想你会喜欢这个小组，因为你提到过想学做饭。你想和我一起试一节课吗？

segments.low: I need to check if there is a free place first.
segments.high: I would need to check whether there is a free place first.

note.zh: 高版本使用“would need to”使语气更委婉，并用“whether”替代“if”更正式。
note.en: The high version uses 'would need to' for a more polite tone and 'whether' instead of 'if' for formality.

translationZh.low: 我需要先检查是否有空位。
translationZh.high: 我需要先检查是否有空位。

segments.low: Let me know what days or times you are free, and I can ask the organiser.
segments.high: Just tell me which days or times suit you, and I will ask the organiser.

note.zh: 高版本用“Just tell me”使语气更轻松，用“suit you”替代“you are free”更地道，并用“will”表示承诺。
note.en: The high version uses 'Just tell me' for a more casual tone, 'suit you' instead of 'you are free' for a more idiomatic expression, and 'will' to indicate a promise.

expressionEdits.before: Let me know what days or times you are free
expressionEdits.after: Just tell me which days or times suit you

explanation.zh: 两种询问都自然；which times suit you 将关注点放在朋友是否方便。
explanation.en: Both questions are natural; which times suit you focuses on the friend’s convenience.

translationZh.low: 告诉我你哪天或什么时候有空，我可以问组织者。
translationZh.high: 告诉我你哪天或什么时候方便，我会问组织者。

segments.low: Hope to see you there!
segments.high: I really hope you can come along!

note.zh: 高版本表达更热情，用“come along”替代“see you there”更口语化。
note.en: The high version is more enthusiastic and uses 'come along' instead of 'see you there' for a more colloquial tone.

translationZh.low: 希望在那里见到你！
translationZh.high: 我真的希望你能来！

segments.low: Best, Alex
segments.high: Take care, Alex

note.zh: 高版本使用更温暖随意的结束语“Take care”，符合非正式信件语气。
note.en: The high version uses the warmer and more casual closing 'Take care', fitting the informal letter tone.

translationZh.low: 祝好，亚历克斯
translationZh.high: 保重，亚历克斯

note.zh: 高版本更清晰地描述了小组性质、活动和个人感受，并恰当地邀请朋友，避免编造未核实的信息。低版本遗漏了“初学者”这一关键信息，且部分表达不够准确。
note.en: The high version more clearly describes the group's nature, activities, and personal feelings, and appropriately invites the friend without inventing unverified details. The low version omits the key detail that the group is for beginners and has some imprecise expressions.

note.zh: 高版本使用更多衔接手段，如“also”的位置调整和“whenever”等，使段落间和句子间过渡更自然。低版本衔接较简单，但整体结构仍清晰。
note.en: The high version uses more cohesive devices, such as the repositioning of 'also' and 'whenever', making transitions between paragraphs and sentences more natural. The low version has simpler cohesion but the overall structure remains clear.

note.zh: 高版本词汇更丰富、准确，如“weekly”、“discuss”、“improve”、“pick up”、“mentioned”等，避免了低版本中的重复和不当用词。
note.en: The high version uses a wider and more precise range of vocabulary, such as 'weekly', 'discuss', 'improve', 'pick up', and 'mentioned', avoiding repetition and inappropriate word choices in the low version.

note.zh: 高版本修正了低版本中的时态错误和主谓一致问题，如“I join”改为“I recently joined”，“Everyone bring”改为“Everyone brings”，并使用了更复杂的结构如“would need to”和“whether”。
note.en: The high version corrects tense errors and subject-verb agreement issues in the low version, such as changing 'I join' to 'I recently joined' and 'Everyone bring' to 'Everyone brings', and uses more complex structures like 'would need to' and 'whether'.

zh: 描述经历时注意使用正确的时态，并包含关键细节如“初学者”。
使用多样化的词汇和短语，如“weekly”、“pick up”、“mentioned”等，使表达更地道。
邀请他人时保持礼貌和鼓励的语气，避免编造未核实的信息。
en: Use correct tenses when describing experiences and include key details such as 'beginner'.
Employ varied vocabulary and phrases like 'weekly', 'pick up', and 'mentioned' for more idiomatic expression.
Maintain a polite and encouraging tone when inviting others and avoid inventing unverified information.

taskAnalysis.zh: 本题要求写一封非正式信，描述烹饪小组、解释喜欢的理由、邀请朋友试课并询问时间。不得编造费用、名额或健康效果。两个范文都完成了任务；高分版语气更自然、语法更准确、用词更地道。
taskAnalysis.en: The task requires an informal letter describing a cooking group, explaining why you enjoy it, inviting a friend to try a session, and asking about availability. Both essays complete the task; the high version is more natural, grammatically accurate, and idiomatic.

role.zh: 开头问候并介绍烹饪小组的基本信息。
role.en: Opening greeting and basic introduction to the cooking group.

analysis.zh: 低分版用一般现在时“join”描述过去事件，时态错误；高分版改用“recently joined”正确表达过去动作。低分版“every week”略显重复，高分版用“weekly”更简洁。低分版主语“Everyone”与动词“bring”不一致，应为“brings”；高分版动词形式正确。整体上，高分版用词更准确，句子更流畅。
analysis.en: The low version uses present tense 'join' for a past event; the high version correctly uses 'recently joined'. 'Every week' is slightly repetitive; 'weekly' is more concise. The low version has subject-verb disagreement: 'Everyone bring' should be 'Everyone brings'; the high version is correct. Overall, the high version is more accurate and fluent.

role.zh: 描述具体活动并解释喜欢这种学习方式的原因。
role.en: Describes specific activities and explains why the writer enjoys this way of learning.

analysis.zh: 低分版“Last time we make”时态错误，应为过去时“made”；高分版使用“made”正确。低分版“talk about what we can do better”表达尚可但不够自然，高分版“discuss what we could improve”更正式且准确。低分版“not like reading a recipe alone”语法正确但平淡，高分版“nothing like”加强语气。低分版“when I am not sure”和“other people help me”略啰嗦，高分版“whenever I am unsure”和“others help me”更简洁。
analysis.en: The low version has tense error: 'Last time we make' should be 'Last time we made'; the high version uses 'made' correctly. 'Talk about what we can do better' is understandable but less natural than 'discuss what we could improve'. 'Not like reading a recipe alone' is correct but weak; 'nothing like' adds emphasis. 'When I am not sure' and 'other people help me' are slightly wordy; 'whenever I am unsure' and 'others help me' are more concise.

role.zh: 进一步说明好处，并邀请朋友参加。
role.en: Further explains benefits and invites the friend to join.

analysis.zh: 低分版“Also, we share simple ideas”中“Also”位置略生硬，高分版“We also share”更自然。低分版“learn new ways”较普通，高分版“pick up new ways”更口语化。低分版“you would like this group”语气较弱，高分版“you would enjoy”更贴切。低分版“you said you want to learn to cook”时态不一致，高分版“you mentioned wanting to learn to cook”更准确。低分版“I need to check if there is a free place first”中“need to”过于直接，高分版“I would need to check whether there is a free place first”更委婉。
analysis.en: In the low version, 'Also, we share' is slightly awkward; 'We also share' is more natural. 'Learn new ways' is plain; 'pick up new ways' is more colloquial. 'You would like this group' is weaker than 'you would enjoy'. 'You said you want to learn to cook' has tense inconsistency; 'you mentioned wanting to learn to cook' is more accurate. 'I need to check' is too direct; 'I would need to check' is more polite.

role.zh: 询问朋友有空的时间并友好结束信件。
role.en: Asks about the friend's availability and ends the letter warmly.

analysis.zh: 低分版“Let me know what days or times you are free”较生硬，高分版“Just tell me which days or times suit you”更友好自然。低分版“I can ask the organiser”中“can”表示能力，高分版“I will ask the organiser”表示意愿，更符合语境。低分版“Hope to see you there!”较平淡，高分版“I really hope you can come along!”更热情。结尾署名低分版用“Best,”较正式，高分版“Take care,”更符合非正式信件风格。
analysis.en: The low version 'Let me know what days or times you are free' is stilted; 'Just tell me which days or times suit you' is friendlier. 'I can ask the organiser' implies ability, while 'I will ask the organiser' expresses intention, which fits better. 'Hope to see you there!' is flat; 'I really hope you can come along!' is warmer. The closing 'Best,' is more formal than 'Take care,' which suits an informal letter.

title.zh: 使用更地道的表达
title.en: Using more idiomatic expressions

explanation.zh: 高分版用“nothing like”替代“not like”，加强了对比语气，使表达更生动。
explanation.en: The high version uses 'nothing like' instead of 'not like' to strengthen the contrast and make the expression more vivid.

title.zh: 使用更口语化的动词短语
title.en: Using more colloquial phrasal verbs

explanation.zh: 高分版用“pick up”替代“learn”，更符合非正式信件的口语风格。
explanation.en: The high version uses 'pick up' instead of 'learn', which is more colloquial and suitable for an informal letter.

title.zh: 使用更委婉的语气
title.en: Using a more polite tone

explanation.zh: 高分版用“I would need to check”替代“I need to check”，显得更委婉，避免过于直接。
explanation.en: The high version uses 'I would need to check' instead of 'I need to check', which sounds more polite and less direct.

mistakes.zh: 低分版第0句“I join”时态错误，应为过去时“joined”，因为加入发生在过去。高分版用“recently joined”正确。
mistakes.en: In the low essay, sentence 0 has a tense error: 'I join' should be 'I joined' because the action happened in the past. The high essay correctly uses 'recently joined'.

mistakes.zh: 低分版第2句“Everyone bring”主谓不一致，主语“Everyone”是单数，动词应为“brings”。高分版用“Everyone brings”正确。
mistakes.en: In the low essay, sentence 2 has subject-verb disagreement: 'Everyone bring' should be 'Everyone brings' because 'everyone' is singular. The high essay correctly uses 'Everyone brings'.

meaning.en: became a member of something a short time ago

usage.zh: 用于描述过去发生的动作，常与一般过去时连用。注意不要与现在完成时混淆，除非强调对现在的影响。
usage.en: Used to describe an action that happened in the past, typically with the simple past tense. Avoid confusing it with the present perfect unless emphasizing a present result.

example.zh: 她最近参加了一个瑜伽班来提高柔韧性。
example.en: She recently joined a yoga class to improve her flexibility.

meaning.en: gather together once every week

usage.zh: 用于描述定期活动，'weekly'是副词，修饰动词'meet'。注意不要与'every week'混淆，两者意思相同但'weekly'更简洁。
usage.en: Used to describe a regular activity. 'Weekly' is an adverb modifying 'meet'. It means the same as 'every week' but is more concise.

example.zh: 读书俱乐部每周在图书馆聚会。
example.en: The book club meets weekly at the library.

meaning.en: carries or provides a recipe for a meeting

usage.zh: 主语是第三人称单数时，动词'bring'要加's'。常用于描述每人贡献某物的情况。
usage.en: When the subject is third person singular, the verb 'bring' takes an 's'. Often used to describe each person contributing something.

example.zh: 每个成员都带一份食谱来参加烹饪活动。
example.en: Each member brings a recipe to the cooking session.

meaning.en: prepared tomato soup by cooking

usage.zh: 过去时态，表示过去完成的动作。注意动词'make'的过去式是'made'。
usage.en: Past tense, indicating a completed action. Note that the past tense of 'make' is 'made'.

example.zh: 昨晚，我从零开始做了番茄汤。
example.en: Last night, I made tomato soup from scratch.

meaning.zh: 讨论我们可以改进的地方
meaning.en: talk about what aspects could be made better

usage.zh: 用于表达对过去活动的反思。'could improve'表示可能性，语气较委婉。
usage.en: Used to reflect on a past activity. 'Could improve' expresses possibility and is more polite.

example.zh: 项目结束后，我们讨论了下一次可以改进的地方。
example.en: After the project, we discussed what we could improve next time.

meaning.en: completely different from

usage.zh: 用于强调两者之间的巨大差异。后面常接名词或动名词。
usage.en: Used to emphasize a great difference between two things. Often followed by a noun or gerund.

example.zh: 和别人一起做饭和独自做饭完全不一样。
example.en: Cooking with others is nothing like cooking alone.

prompt.zh: 在这一虚构情境中，你将离开一周，希望朋友 Morgan 帮忙查看公寓。两盆室内植物需在该周浇水一次，还需将信箱中的信收进屋。写信给 Morgan：①说明请求和为何向朋友求助；②清楚说明这两项任务；③询问是否方便帮忙，若同意再商量交接钥匙。尚未确定具体出行日期或交接，不编造地址、门禁码、紧急事件或额外家务。使用感激的非正式语气，不少于 150 词，以 Dear Morgan, 开头。

title.zh: 非正式信：请朋友临时照看住处
title.en: Informal Letter: Asking a Friend to Check Your Home

segments.low: Dear Morgan, I hope you are well.
segments.high: Dear Morgan, I hope you're doing well.

note.zh: 将正式问候改为更口语化的缩略形式，更符合非正式信函语气。
note.en: Changes the formal greeting to a more conversational contraction, fitting the informal letter tone.

expressionEdits.before: I hope you are well.
expressionEdits.after: I hope you're doing well.

explanation.zh: 使用缩略形式和非正式短语，语气更自然友好。
explanation.en: Using a contraction and informal phrase makes the greeting sound more natural and friendly.

translationZh.low: 亲爱的 Morgan，希望你一切都好。
translationZh.high: 亲爱的 Morgan，希望你最近过得不错。

segments.low: I am going away for one week and I need a favour.
segments.high: I'll be away for a week, and I'd like to ask a favour.

note.zh: 用更委婉的请求表达，显得更有礼貌。
note.en: Uses a more polite, tentative request expression.

expressionEdits.before: I need a favour.
expressionEdits.after: I'd like to ask a favour.

explanation.zh: 从直接陈述需求改为礼貌的请求句式。
explanation.en: Changes from a direct statement of need to a polite request formula.

translationZh.low: 我要离开一周，需要请你帮忙。
translationZh.high: 我要离开一周，想请你帮个忙。

segments.low: Because you are a careful and reliable friend, I want to ask you to check my flat.
segments.high: Since you're someone I can trust to be careful and reliable, I'm hoping you might check my flat.

note.zh: 用更自然的口语连接词和委婉表达，句子更流畅。
note.en: Uses a more natural spoken connector and tentative phrasing for smoother flow.

translationZh.low: 因为你是一个细心可靠的朋友，我想请你检查我的公寓。
translationZh.high: 因为你是我信任的细心可靠的人，我希望你能帮我看看公寓。

segments.low: I would feel better knowing that someone I trust could look in while I am away.
segments.high: Knowing that a trusted friend could look in while I'm away would put my mind at ease.

note.zh: 用更地道的习语表达安心，句子更简洁。
note.en: Uses an idiomatic expression for reassurance and a more concise sentence.

translationZh.low: 如果知道有信任的人在我离开时照看，我会感觉更好。
translationZh.high: 知道有信任的朋友在我离开时照看，会让我安心。

segments.low: There are two indoor plants in the living room. They need watering once during that week. Please give them a little water but not too much.
segments.high: There are two indoor plants in the living room that need watering once while I'm gone. Just give them a modest amount of water, but be careful not to overdo it.

note.zh: 将两个短句合并为定语从句，指令表达更简洁自然。
note.en: Combines two short sentences into a relative clause and uses more natural instructional language.

expressionEdits.before: There are two indoor plants in the living room. They need watering once during that week.
expressionEdits.after: There are two indoor plants in the living room that need watering once while I'm gone.

explanation.zh: 用定语从句合并句子，避免重复主语，衔接更紧密。
explanation.en: Uses a relative clause to combine sentences, avoiding repetition and improving cohesion.

translationZh.low: 客厅里有两盆室内植物。它们需要在那一周浇水一次。请给它们浇一点水，但不要太多。
translationZh.high: 客厅里有两盆室内植物，我不在时需要浇一次水。只需浇适量水，但注意不要浇太多。

segments.low: Also, letters should be brought in from the mailbox.
segments.high: In addition, could you bring in any letters from the mailbox?

note.zh: 将被动语态改为礼貌的疑问句请求，更符合信函语境。
note.en: Changes passive voice to a polite question form, more appropriate for a letter request.

expressionEdits.before: letters should be brought in from the mailbox.
expressionEdits.after: could you bring in any letters from the mailbox?

explanation.zh: 从被动陈述改为主动疑问句，直接向对方提出请求。
explanation.en: Changes from passive statement to active question, directly addressing the recipient.

translationZh.low: 还有，信件应该从信箱里取进来。
translationZh.high: 另外，你能把信箱里的信件取进来吗？

segments.low: Please take them inside and put them on the table.
segments.high: If you could place them on the table inside, that would be great.

note.zh: 用更礼貌的条件句式，语气更委婉。
note.en: Uses a more polite conditional structure to soften the request.

translationZh.low: 请把它们拿进来放在桌子上。
translationZh.high: 如果你能把它们放在里面的桌子上，那就太好了。

segments.low: There is no other housework for you to do, so I hope this will not take much of your time.
segments.high: Those would be the only tasks, so I hope the visit wouldn't take up too much of your time.

note.zh: 用更简洁的指代和自然表达，避免重复。
note.en: Uses more concise referencing and natural phrasing to avoid repetition.

translationZh.low: 没有其他家务需要你做，所以我希望这不会占用你太多时间。
translationZh.high: 这些就是全部任务，所以我希望这次拜访不会占用你太多时间。

segments.low: Would you be able to help me with this? If you agree, we can arrange a key handover. I can give you the key before I leave.
segments.high: Do you think you'd be able to help with this? If so, we can sort out a time to hand over the key before I go.

note.zh: 合并重复信息，使用更口语化的表达。
note.en: Merges repetitive information and uses more colloquial expressions.

translationZh.low: 你能帮我这个忙吗？如果你同意，我们可以安排钥匙交接。我可以在离开前把钥匙给你。
translationZh.high: 你觉得你能帮我这个忙吗？如果可以，我们可以在离开前安排个时间交接钥匙。

segments.low: Thank you for considering it. I really appreciate your help.
segments.high: Thanks so much for considering it—I'd really appreciate your help.

note.zh: 用破折号连接两个短句，表达更紧凑自然。
note.en: Uses a dash to connect two short sentences for a more compact, natural expression.

translationZh.low: 感谢你考虑这件事。我非常感激你的帮助。
translationZh.high: 非常感谢你考虑这件事——我真的很感激你的帮助。

segments.low: Please do not feel that you must say yes if you are busy that week. Best wishes, Alex
segments.high: Please don't feel obliged to say yes if that week is already busy for you. Best wishes, Alex

note.zh: 用更精确的短语表达，避免误解。
note.en: Uses a more precise phrase to avoid ambiguity.

expressionEdits.before: Please do not feel that you must say yes if you are busy that week.
expressionEdits.after: Please don't feel obliged to say yes if that week is already busy for you.

explanation.zh: 用更地道的表达替换直译，语义更准确。
explanation.en: Replaces a literal expression with a more idiomatic one for clearer meaning.

translationZh.low: 如果你那周很忙，请不必勉强答应。祝好，Alex
translationZh.high: 如果那周你已经很忙，请不必觉得有义务答应。祝好，Alex

note.zh: 两个版本均涵盖所有要点：说明请求及原因、描述两项任务、询问能否帮忙并提及钥匙交接。高版本在表达上更委婉自然，但低版本也完整回应了任务。未出现无关信息。
note.en: Both versions cover all bullet points: explaining the request and reason, describing the two tasks, asking about help, and mentioning key handover. The high version phrases things more politely and naturally, but the low version also fully addresses the task. No irrelevant information is included.

note.zh: 高版本使用更多连接手段（如 since, if so, 破折号）和指代词，段落内部衔接更流畅。低版本句子较短，部分地方重复，但整体逻辑清晰，分段合理。
note.en: The high version uses more cohesive devices (e.g., since, if so, dashes) and referencing, making paragraphs flow more smoothly. The low version has shorter sentences and some repetition, but the overall logic is clear and paragraphing is appropriate.

note.zh: 高版本词汇更丰富地道，如 put my mind at ease, sort out, hand over, feel obliged 等。低版本用词基本准确但较简单，如 give, arrange, must say yes。整体词汇满足任务要求。
note.en: The high version uses richer, more idiomatic vocabulary, such as put my mind at ease, sort out, hand over, feel obliged. The low version uses mostly accurate but simpler words like give, arrange, must say yes. Overall vocabulary meets the task requirements.

note.zh: 高版本句式更多样，包括条件句、定语从句、疑问句等，语法准确。低版本以简单句和主动语态为主，有一处被动语态使用略显生硬，但无严重语法错误。
note.en: The high version uses a wider range of structures, including conditionals, relative clauses, and question forms, with accurate grammar. The low version relies mainly on simple sentences and active voice, with one slightly awkward passive construction, but no serious grammatical errors.

zh: 使用更口语化的缩略形式和地道短语，让非正式信函语气更自然。
通过合并句子和运用连接词，减少重复，增强段落衔接。
用条件句和委婉表达提出请求，显得更礼貌得体。
en: Use contractions and idiomatic phrases to make informal letters sound more natural.
Combine sentences and use linking words to reduce repetition and improve cohesion.
Make requests more politely by using conditional structures and hedging expressions.

taskAnalysis.zh: 这是一个非正式GT书信任务，要求向朋友Morgan求助照看公寓。题目明确要求解释请求、描述两项任务、询问是否帮忙并提议交接钥匙。语气需感激非正式，不编造细节。高分回答应自然、简洁、具体，避免过度正式或冗余。
taskAnalysis.en: This is an informal GT letter task asking a friend for help checking a flat. The prompt requires explaining the request, describing two tasks, and asking about help with a key handover. The tone should be appreciative and informal without inventing details. A high-scoring answer should be natural, concise, and specific.

role.zh: 开头段落：问候、说明请求原因、描述第一项任务（给植物浇水）。
role.en: Opening paragraph: greeting, explaining the request and why asking this friend, and describing the first task (watering plants).

analysis.zh: 该段完成了两项任务：解释请求并描述第一项任务。高分版本用更自然的口语表达（如'I'll be away'而非'I am going away'），并且将请求与信任朋友的理由结合得更流畅。低分版本句子略显生硬，如'Because you are a careful and reliable friend, I want to ask you'结构较直接。高分版本通过'Since you're someone I can trust to be careful and reliable'更委婉地表达信任，同时'put my mind at ease'是地道表达。
analysis.en: This paragraph covers two tasks: explaining the request and describing the first task. The high version uses more natural spoken expressions (e.g., 'I'll be away' instead of 'I am going away') and integrates the reason for asking with trust in the friend more smoothly. The low version has slightly stilted sentences, such as 'Because you are a careful and reliable friend, I want to ask you.' The high version uses 'Since you're someone I can trust to be careful and reliable' to express trust more politely, and 'put my mind at ease' is an idiomatic phrase.

role.zh: 中间段落：描述第二项任务（取信），并强调没有额外家务。
role.en: Middle paragraph: describing the second task (bringing in letters) and emphasizing no extra chores.

analysis.zh: 该段描述第二项任务并说明没有其他事情。高分版本使用礼貌请求句式'could you bring in...'和'If you could place...'，语气更委婉。低分版本使用被动语态'letters should be brought in'，显得间接且不够自然。高分版本用'Those would be the only tasks'简洁总结，而低分版本'There is no other housework for you to do'略啰嗦。
analysis.en: This paragraph describes the second task and clarifies there are no other chores. The high version uses polite request structures like 'could you bring in...' and 'If you could place...', making the tone more courteous. The low version uses the passive voice 'letters should be brought in', which is indirect and less natural. The high version summarizes with 'Those would be the only tasks', while the low version 'There is no other housework for you to do' is slightly wordy.

role.zh: 结尾段落：询问是否帮忙、提议交接钥匙、表达感谢并给予拒绝空间。
role.en: Closing paragraph: asking if they can help, offering key handover, expressing thanks, and giving space to decline.

analysis.zh: 该段完成询问和感谢。高分版本使用'Do you think you'd be able to help?'更口语化，'sort out a time to hand over the key'比'arrange a key handover'更自然。低分版本'Please do not feel that you must say yes if you are busy that week'稍显正式，高分版本'Please don't feel obliged to say yes if that week is already busy for you'更符合朋友间语气。
analysis.en: This paragraph addresses the request and thanks. The high version uses 'Do you think you'd be able to help?' which is more conversational, and 'sort out a time to hand over the key' is more natural than 'arrange a key handover.' The low version 'Please do not feel that you must say yes if you are busy that week' is slightly formal, while the high version 'Please don't feel obliged to say yes if that week is already busy for you' matches the friendly tone better.

title.zh: 使用委婉请求句式
title.en: Using polite request structures

explanation.zh: 高分版本在描述任务时使用'could you bring in...'和'If you could place...'，比低分版本的被动语态或直接命令更礼貌自然。这种句式在非正式书信中既能清晰传达要求，又保持友好语气。
explanation.en: The high version uses 'could you bring in...' and 'If you could place...' when describing tasks, which is more polite and natural than the passive voice or direct commands in the low version. Such structures convey requests clearly while maintaining a friendly tone in informal letters.

title.zh: 采用口语化缩略形式
title.en: Using conversational contractions

explanation.zh: 高分版本大量使用缩略形式，如'I'll', 'you're', 'I'm', 'don't'，使语言更接近日常对话。低分版本使用完整形式'I am', 'you are'，显得稍正式。非正式信件中适当使用缩略形式可增强亲切感。
explanation.en: The high version uses many contractions such as 'I'll', 'you're', 'I'm', 'don't', making the language closer to everyday conversation. The low version uses full forms like 'I am', 'you are', which sound slightly formal. Using contractions appropriately in informal letters can enhance friendliness.

title.zh: 使用地道习语
title.en: Using idiomatic expressions

explanation.zh: 高分版本使用'put my mind at ease'这一习语来表达安心，比低分版本'I would feel better'更生动地道。习语能提升语言的自然度和表现力，但需确保使用准确。
explanation.en: The high version uses the idiom 'put my mind at ease' to express reassurance, which is more vivid and idiomatic than the low version's 'I would feel better.' Idioms can enhance naturalness and expressiveness, but they must be used accurately.

mistakes.zh: 低分版本中'Because you are a careful and reliable friend, I want to ask you to check my flat.'句式直接且略显生硬。高分版本改为'Since you're someone I can trust to be careful and reliable, I'm hoping you might check my flat.'，用'Since'引导原因更自然，'I'm hoping you might'比'I want to ask you'更委婉礼貌。
mistakes.en: In the low version, 'Because you are a careful and reliable friend, I want to ask you to check my flat.' is direct and slightly stiff. The high version changes it to 'Since you're someone I can trust to be careful and reliable, I'm hoping you might check my flat.', using 'Since' for a more natural cause, and 'I'm hoping you might' is more polite than 'I want to ask you'.

mistakes.zh: 低分版本中'Also, letters should be brought in from the mailbox.'使用被动语态，显得间接且不自然。高分版本改为'In addition, could you bring in any letters from the mailbox?'，用主动语态和礼貌请求，更符合朋友间交流。
mistakes.en: In the low version, 'Also, letters should be brought in from the mailbox.' uses the passive voice, which sounds indirect and unnatural. The high version changes it to 'In addition, could you bring in any letters from the mailbox?', using active voice and a polite request, which is more appropriate for communication between friends.

meaning.zh: 让我安心，消除我的担忧
meaning.en: to make me feel less worried or anxious

usage.zh: 这是一个固定短语，通常用于表达某事让人放心。主语通常是使人安心的事物或行为，后面可接'about'引出具体内容。注意不要与'put my mind to'（专心于）混淆。
usage.en: This is a fixed phrase used to express that something makes one feel reassured. The subject is usually the thing or action that causes relief, and it can be followed by 'about' to specify the concern. Do not confuse with 'put my mind to' (to concentrate on).

collocations: put my mind at ease about something

example.zh: 听说你会来查看公寓真的会让我安心。
example.en: Hearing that you'll check on the flat would really put my mind at ease.

meaning.zh: 适度的量，不太多也不太少
meaning.en: a moderate quantity, not too much or too little

usage.zh: 'modest'在此表示'适度的'，常用于描述数量或程度。'a modest amount of'后接不可数名词，如water, money, time。避免与' modest'表示'谦虚的'含义混淆。
usage.en: 'Modest' here means 'moderate', often used to describe quantity or degree. 'A modest amount of' is followed by uncountable nouns like water, money, time. Avoid confusing with the meaning of 'modest' as 'humble'.

example.zh: 请给每株植物加适量的肥料。
example.en: Please add a modest amount of fertilizer to each plant.

meaning.en: to do too much of something, to exaggerate

usage.zh: 'overdo'是及物动词，'it'指代前面提到的动作。常用于口语，表示警告不要过量。可以说'overdo the watering'或'overdo it'。注意过去式为'overdid'，过去分词'overdone'。
usage.en: 'Overdo' is a transitive verb, and 'it' refers to the action mentioned before. Commonly used in spoken English to warn against excess. You can say 'overdo the watering' or 'overdo it'. Note past tense 'overdid', past participle 'overdone'.

example.zh: 注意不要给植物施肥过量。
example.en: Be careful not to overdo it with the plant food.

meaning.en: to arrange or resolve something

usage.zh: 'sort out'是常见短语动词，意为'安排'或'解决'。可接名词或动名词，如'sort out a time', 'sort out the details'。在非正式语境中常用，比'arrange'更口语化。
usage.en: 'Sort out' is a common phrasal verb meaning 'to arrange' or 'to resolve'. It can be followed by a noun or gerund, e.g., 'sort out a time', 'sort out the details'. It is more informal than 'arrange' and common in spoken English.

example.zh: 我们下周找个时间见面吧。
example.en: Let's sort out a day to meet next week.

meaning.en: to give something to someone else, often formally

usage.zh: 'hand over'意为'移交'，常用于交接物品或责任。可分开使用，如'hand the key over'。在信中用于钥匙交接，比'give'更具体。注意与'hand in'（提交）区别。
usage.en: 'Hand over' means to give something to someone else, often formally. It can be separated, e.g., 'hand the key over'. In this context, it refers to transferring the key, more specific than 'give'. Distinguish from 'hand in' (to submit).

example.zh: 我们见面时我会把备用钥匙交给你。
example.en: I'll hand over the spare key when we meet.

meaning.en: to feel that one must do something because of duty or pressure

usage.zh: 'feel obliged to do something'表示感到有义务做某事，常因道德或社会压力。在否定句中用于告诉对方不必勉强。比'feel you must'更委婉。注意'obliged'是形容词，常与'feel'连用。
usage.en: 'Feel obliged to do something' means to feel that one must do something due to duty or pressure. In negative sentences, it is used to tell someone not to feel forced. It is more polite than 'feel you must'. Note 'obliged' is an adjective often used with 'feel'.

example.zh: 如果你累了，不必勉强留下。
example.en: Please don't feel obliged to stay if you're tired.

prompt.zh: 在这一虚构情境中，朋友 Casey 帮你打包书籍并给纸箱贴标签，协助搬家。你现已拆箱并在新家安顿下来。写信给 Casey：①感谢这项具体帮助；②解释它怎样让搬家更轻松，并说说安顿情况；③邀请朋友来吃顿便饭，询问何时有空。不要编造付费服务、礼物金额、地址、具体日期或已确定的来访。使用温暖的非正式语气，不少于 150 词，以 Dear Casey, 开头。

title.zh: 非正式信：感谢朋友帮助搬家
title.en: Informal Letter: Thanking a Friend for Moving Help

segments.low: Dear Casey, I want to say thank you for helping me with the move.
segments.high: Dear Casey, Thank you so much for all your help with the move.

note.zh: 将简单的感谢改为更热情、更全面的表达，增强温暖语气。
note.en: The simple thanks is replaced with a warmer, more comprehensive expression.

expressionEdits.before: I want to say thank you for helping me with the move.
expressionEdits.after: Thank you so much for all your help with the move.

explanation.zh: 用更直接、更热情的感谢短语，并强调所有帮助。
explanation.en: Uses a more direct and warmer thanking phrase, and emphasizes all the help.

translationZh.low: 亲爱的凯西，我想对你说谢谢，感谢你帮我搬家。
translationZh.high: 亲爱的凯西，非常感谢你帮我搬家所做的一切。

segments.low: Packing all my books was a big job, and you did it very good.
segments.high: Packing all those books was a huge job, and you did it brilliantly.

note.zh: 修正副词形式，并将形容词升级为更强烈的表达。
note.en: Corrects the adverb form and upgrades the adjective to a stronger expression.

expressionEdits.before: you did it very good
expressionEdits.after: you did it brilliantly

explanation.zh: 将形容词 good 改为副词 brilliantly，并强化程度。
explanation.en: Changes the adjective 'good' to the adverb 'brilliantly' and intensifies the meaning.

expressionEdits.before: a big job
expressionEdits.after: a huge job

explanation.zh: 用更强烈的形容词 huge 替代 big，突出任务艰巨。
explanation.en: Replaces 'big' with the stronger adjective 'huge' to emphasize the difficulty.

translationZh.low: 打包我所有的书是一项大工作，你做得非常好。
translationZh.high: 打包那些书是一项艰巨的工作，你做得非常出色。

segments.low: Also you put labels on the boxes, so I know what is inside.
segments.high: You also labelled the boxes clearly, so I could see exactly what was inside.

note.zh: 调整句子结构，增加副词 clearly 和更精确的表达，使逻辑更清晰。
note.en: Restructures the sentence, adds the adverb 'clearly' and a more precise expression for clearer logic.

translationZh.low: 而且你在箱子上贴了标签，所以我知道里面是什么。
translationZh.high: 你还清晰地给箱子贴了标签，这样我就能确切知道里面是什么。
